member.name: T:ODDGames.Scripting.Binding.AsyncLowering
member.summary:
AST-to-AST rewrite that turns every async method into a stub + a synthesized state-machine ScriptType. Runs between SemanticAnalyzer and Emitter.
v1 scope. Supports: await expr; and var x = await expr; at statement level; await as a sub-expression in binary, member, call, index, cast, paren, unary expressions; if/while with awaits anywhere in the condition or body. The body is linearised into a CFG of "basic blocks" (no awaits inside) and assembled as while (true) { if (__pc == K) {...} ... } inside the synthesized MoveNext method.
NOT supported (errors): await inside try/catch/finally; await inside a lambda; await on the RHS of compound assignment (+= etc.); await inside short-circuit && / || / ?:; await inside foreach / for / do-while.

member.name: T:ODDGames.Scripting.Binding.IteratorLowering
member.summary:
AST-to-AST rewrite for iterator methods (those containing yield return / yield break). The iterator method is replaced with a stub that constructs a state-machine ScriptType and wraps it in a runtime adapter implementing IEnumerable<object>.
v1 lazy mode. The body is desugared (for/do-while/foreach → while-with-gotos), then all locals are promoted to fields on the synthesised state-machine type, and the body becomes the MoveNext() method. Each yield return X turns into __current = X; __pc = N; return true; L_N: ;. A __pc-keyed dispatch at the top of MoveNext resumes at the right label.
Eager fallback. Iterators whose body contains try/catch/finally or nested lambdas use the legacy eager rewrite (materialise to a List<object>), because the goto-based linearisation can't safely thread through exception handlers in v1. Observable side-effect ordering may differ from real C# for the eager path.

member.summary:
Per-call-site cache slot used by dynamic dispatch opcodes (CallInstanceDynamic, LoadMemberDynamic, IndexGet, etc.). On the first hit, the VM resolves the member via reflection and writes + into the slot. member.summary:
Binds script uses of 's members (also reached through derived types) to a host type's same-named public static members, so scripts write the ordinary API and get the host's safe behaviour.
A static method, property or field binds to the target's static of the same name (and fitting signature).
An instance method binds to a target static method whose first parameter is the receiver: go.AddComponent<T>() runs Target.AddComponent<T>(GameObject self).
With , scripts may also call the members unqualified, as code in a class deriving from would (Destroy(obj), StartCoroutine(Run())); those bind to target static methods taking exactly the script's arguments. A redirected member itself never runs: when no target member fits, the use is an error whatever the member rules say. Scripts cannot name the target type; its members run only through redirects. A target that takes objects the script may not change belongs in (it then checks them itself).
